headline: Microsoft surged 5.7% last night while Google slipped 2.2% — big divergence in your US tech holdings — and the RBA held rates steady today, giving the ASX a lift.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft had a strong night last session, jumping 5.7% — likely driven by continued market enthusiasm around its AI products and cloud growth story. The market is increasingly favouring Microsoft's AI narrative over Google's, which helps explain why MSFT surged while GOOG fell on the same night. Still down about 16% on your total investment though, so this is a welcome bounce rather than a full recovery.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped 2.2% last session. Alphabet's earnings are in focus this week, and traders may be rotating into Microsoft's stronger AI story ahead of the results. Worth watching closely — earnings could be the catalyst that reverses this or deepens the drop.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE had a solid session today, up 1.5%. Emerging markets got a boost from a broadly positive ASX session and some softening in the US dollar. Good to see some green here after a long flat stretch — you're essentially back to breakeven on this one.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS closed up about 1% today, riding the tailwinds from last night's reasonable US session and a positive ASX mood following the RBA rate hold. Tracking the broad US market, so it benefited from the same momentum that pushed MSFT higher.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI ticked up 0.9% today — a small positive in what's otherwise been a tough run for this ETF. It holds a basket of global AI companies, so it catches some of the Microsoft tailwind, though Google's dip drags a little. Still down about 6% overall on your investment.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS edged up 0.8% today as lithium stocks showed signs of life on the ASX. Multiple outlets are noting a lithium sector rebound, with Pilbara leading the charge — but this follows a prolonged downturn and you're still down nearly 25% on your investment here. The recovery is early days.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG rose 0.7% today, a steady and unsurprising move given the broadly positive ASX session after the RBA kept rates on hold. As a diversified fund holding global and Australian shares, it absorbs both the MSFT tailwind and the GOOG headwind — net result is a modest positive day.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 0.7% today despite oil (WTI crude) actually ticking up slightly last night. Energy stocks can lag oil price moves by a session, and broader sector sentiment remains cautious with no major supply shock in play. A minor move — nothing alarming.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two was essentially flat last session, down just 0.08%. GTA 6 news continues to swirl — console pre-orders are locked in for a November 2026 release, but reports suggest disc editions won't be available at launch, which took a little shine off. Overall the GTA 6 hype is keeping the stock well supported near current levels.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Earnings in focus this week
watch_today.detail: Alphabet is on the earnings calendar this week (likely Tuesday US time, which is Wednesday morning AEST). Last night's 2.2% drop suggests the market is a little nervous going in. A strong result could snap back the slide — a miss could push it lower. Given your small position (only ~$110 AUD value), the risk is manageable, but worth watching closely.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Big bounce — but still down 16% overall
watch_today.detail: Microsoft's 5.7% jump last night is the biggest single-day move in your portfolio. It's being driven by AI momentum and the market favouring Microsoft's cloud + AI story. That said, you're still sitting on a $64 AUD loss overall on this position. No reason to sell into strength, but don't mistake one good night for a full recovery.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium rebound underway — but stay cautious
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals edged up today and multiple analysts are calling a lithium sector rebound. However, you're still down nearly 25% on your PLS investment. The rebound is early and lithium prices remain subdued globally. Watch for follow-through this week before reading too much into today's small gain.

watch_today.title: RBA held interest rates today — good news for the ASX
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia left interest rates unchanged at today's meeting, giving relief to mortgage holders and boosting confidence across the sharemarket. The ASX 200 closed up 0.68% to 8,823. Rate holds are generally positive for growth assets like your VDHG, VTS, and VGE holdings.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 November release locked in via pre-orders
watch_today.detail: Console pre-orders for GTA 6 have confirmed a November 2026 release window, keeping the hype train on track. However, reports from a Rockstar source suggest physical disc editions won't be available at launch, which disappointed some fans. The stock barely moved last session (-0.08%), suggesting the market had mostly priced this in. Hold and watch for any release date confirmation closer to November.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a solid session today, closing up 0.68% to 8,823 after the RBA held interest rates steady — giving investors one less thing to worry about. Last night on Wall Street, it was a split tape: the S&P 500 was essentially flat (-0.05%) and the NASDAQ dipped 0.24%, but the big story was Microsoft rocketing 5.7% while Google fell 2.2%. Gold was steady near all-time highs around US$4,077, and oil ticked up slightly to US$69.61. The Aussie dollar is holding firm at 68.98 US cents.

indicators.note: Closed up strongly today after RBA held rates steady

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Essentially flat last night — mixed signals across sectors

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Slight dip last night despite Microsoft's big surge — Google's drop was a drag

indicators.note: Edged higher — no major supply news, steady demand picture

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Virtually unchanged — still near record highs, safe-haven demand steady

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Barely moved — RBA hold was already priced in by the market

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is the RBA holding interest rates steady, giving mortgage holders a breather and lifting the ASX. The Albanese government also cranked up pressure on tech giants with a massive penalty increase for social media platforms that allow under-16s on their platforms.

stories.title: RBA holds interest rates — mortgage holders get relief
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank left the cash rate unchanged at today's meeting, meaning no extra pain for people with variable-rate mortgages. The ASX responded positively, closing up 0.68%. It also signals the RBA thinks inflation is cooling enough that further hikes aren't needed right now — good news for growth assets like shares and property.

stories.title: RBA prepares 'fire drills' for the next COVID-like crisis
stories.why_it_matters: RBA Assistant Governor Christopher Kent has flagged the central bank is actively war-gaming scenarios for the next major economic shock — think another pandemic or global financial crisis. The RBA wants to be better prepared with policy tools and communication strategies so it can respond faster and more effectively. For investors, it's reassuring that the central bank is thinking ahead rather than being caught flat-footed.

stories.title: Albanese Government doubles penalty to $99m for tech giants over under-16 social media rules
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government has doubled the maximum fine for tech platforms that allow children under 16 to use social media, lifting it to $99 million. This puts serious financial pressure on companies like Meta (Facebook/Instagram), TikTok, and Snapchat to enforce age verification. For Australian investors with exposure to global tech, it's a reminder that regulatory risk for social platforms is real and growing — though the direct impact on your GOOG holding (YouTube) would depend on enforcement scope.

stories.title: CBA in focus after RBA rate decision
stories.why_it_matters: Commonwealth Bank (CBA) is in the spotlight following today's RBA hold. When the RBA keeps rates steady, bank net interest margins (the gap between what banks charge borrowers and pay depositors) can come under pressure as competition for deposits intensifies. CBA is the ASX's largest stock, so its direction often pulls the broader index. Analysts are watching whether CBA passes through any relief to mortgage customers or holds firm to protect margins.

ai.summary: Today's AI news is dominated by the regulation theme — governments and researchers around the world are wrestling with how to govern AI before it outpaces the rulebook. Nothing groundbreaking in terms of new AI capabilities today, but the regulatory landscape is shifting fast and it matters for your GXAI.AX holding.

stories.title: GDPR — not the EU's AI Act — was what actually delayed AI in Europe
stories.why_it_matters: New research shows it was Europe's existing privacy law — the GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation, which restricts how companies collect and use personal data) — rather than the new AI Act that actually caused major AI companies to delay releasing frontier models in Europe. This matters because it means AI regulation is more complex than just passing AI-specific laws; existing rules can have just as big an impact. For investors in AI ETFs like GXAI.AX, European regulatory risk is real and ongoing.

stories.title: Calls for AI regulation grow as media faces a defining moment
stories.why_it_matters: Media organisations are increasingly calling for AI regulation, particularly around AI-generated content and deepfakes that could be mistaken for real journalism. The core concern is that without guardrails, AI tools will flood the internet with misinformation. For Big Tech companies like Google (which owns YouTube) and Microsoft (which owns LinkedIn and AI products), increased content regulation could mean higher compliance costs ahead.

stories.title: AI regulation redefines European retail
stories.why_it_matters: European retailers are having to rethink how they use AI tools for pricing, personalisation, and logistics as the EU's AI Act starts to bite. High-risk AI uses (like automated hiring decisions or credit scoring) now require strict documentation and human oversight. For global AI companies supplying these tools, Europe's rules are setting a de-facto global standard — which increases costs but also creates a competitive moat for companies that get compliance right early.

sport.summary: Wimbledon kicked off today with the big guns — Sinner and Djokovic both in action. NRL Round 17 wrapped up with some controversy, and the AFL served up a record-breaking milestone from Fremantle. Round 18 NRL kicks off Friday night.

stories.title: Wimbledon 2026 begins: Sinner and Djokovic headline opening day
stories.why_it_matters: The Championships at Wimbledon got underway today with world number one Jannik Sinner and tennis legend Novak Djokovic both taking to the grass on Day 1. Sinner is defending his 2025 Wimbledon crown, as is Iga Swiatek on the women's side. Djokovic, chasing history, has drawn inspiration from Serena Williams' longevity as he targets a record-breaking Wimbledon title haul. Madison Keys, fresh off her 2025 Australian Open win, is also one to watch.

stories.title: Controversial Bunker call mars Raiders win in Round 17
stories.why_it_matters: The Raiders claimed victory in Round 17 but the result was overshadowed by a controversial Bunker (video review) call that ruled out what many thought was a legitimate try. Coach Ricky Stuart also made a 'brutal' mid-game tactical move that drew plenty of attention. The result has the Raiders in decent shape heading into Round 18, where they have the bye — giving them a week to regroup.

stories.title: Fremantle set record for longest winning streak by a major WA sporting club
stories.why_it_matters: Fremantle Dockers have set a new record for the longest winning streak by any major WA sporting club, doing so by defeating the Gold Coast Suns. The Dockers are flying in 2026 and this milestone cements their status as genuine AFL premiership contenders. Tough news for local Gold Coast fans — the Suns continue to struggle against top-eight competition.

stories.title: Melbourne Storm sign two players, fourth star could miss rest of season
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Storm have signed two players from NRL rivals ahead of the second half of the season, bolstering their depth. However, a fourth Storm star is in doubt and could miss the rest of the 2026 season — a significant blow to a club pushing for the title. The article doesn't name the player specifically, but the injury is described as serious enough to end their season.
